abstract: We test whether numerical stain-decomposition diagnostics improve source-specific strength assignment for residual-preserving augmentation. An eight-class HMU experiment uses an exact-duplicate-controlled image split without verified patient mapping. A five-group HiESD experiment uses a quality-screened patient-grouped subset and ImageNet-pretrained ResNet18. Standard, fixed, uniformly weaker, global shuffled, adaptive and within-class shuffled controls share seed-specific initialization and bounded training rules. Across three seeds, HMU adaptive validation macro-F1 is 0.6836 versus global shuffled 0.6890; HiESD adaptive is 0.7131 versus global shuffled 0.7350. On the frozen test of 1613 patches from 7 reserved patients, adaptive mean macro-F1 is 0.6602 versus within-class shuffled 0.6749. The prespecified difference is -0.0147, with descriptive patient-cluster interval [-0.0376, +0.0069]. A positive adaptive-minus-within-class validation contrast reverses on the reserved cases. These data do not establish diagnostic-assignment benefit. Independent prediction audits support numerical integrity; coarse masks, rare-class support and seven test-patient clusters limit generalization. Reweighting illustrates known metric behavior, not a new metric. Algorithmic novelty and clinical benefit are unconfirmed.
within_text: Adaptive-minus-within-class-shuffled validation differences are +0.0044, +0.0135, +0.0026; mean +0.0068, exploratory three-seed t interval [-0.0077, +0.0214]. This post-hoc validation contrast does not establish superiority over standard or global shuffled augmentation.

test.bootstrap_convention: Fixed five classes, zero_division=0 even if a class is absent in a draw; small-cluster interval is descriptive and may be unstable.
test.scope: Frozen final test on reserved public-release patients; not independent cross-hospital external testing, not clinical validation. No tuning after test access.

test_text: The frozen final test completed on 1613 patches from 7 reserved patients. The prespecified adaptive-minus-within-class-shuffled mean macro-F1 difference was -0.0147, with descriptive patient-cluster interval [-0.0376, +0.0069]. Of 1,000 cluster draws, 31 lacked at least one class; fixed five-class zero-division-zero scoring was retained. Only 7 usable patient clusters limit precision. All models were frozen before acquisition; no tuning follows test access. This is held-out public-release testing, not independent clinical external validation.
